Five Point’s, brief, abridged history:

Five Points was the notorious slum in NYC that housed mainly immigrants in the 1800s. The name came from the “five point” created by the streets in Manhattan. The slum’s beginning started with the filling of the Collect Pond, which was once a source of fresh water for the residents in NYC, but, with time and pollution, became toxic and unusable (trivia: Canal Street is named because it was the route for the canal that cleared this pond). However, the landfill was poorly engineered and the homes that were built on top of it started shifting in their foundation. Methane also escaped from the ground. The area’s middle and upper class residents vacated the area.

The cheap rent for the area attracted immigrants and emancipated African American slaves starting in the early 1800s. It reached a height in 1840s with the Irish immigrants escaping the potato famine. There was racial tension between these two primary groups of people who lived in the area (status and job related), which escalated into the Draft Riots (started as a rebellion against the drafts, but ultimately turned into a race riot due to lingering tensions).

The area was known for the high population density, horrible conditions (diseases, mortality, smell), depraved activity (prostitution, sexual activity), corruption, and violence (homicides). It is rumored that it had the highest murder rate in the world. According to an urban legend, there was up to 15 murders a night in the Old Brewery (featured in Gangs of New York). There were many diseases that struck the residents, notably cholera (which people justified as being punishment for the depraved activities and religious belief of the area).

In popular culture, the area is known for being the setting for the movie Gangs of New York. Movie was inaccurate in so many ways, but it perfectly captured the slanted, dirty look of the area.
